findings.passage: The law changed. So, now you have to have a drivers license, a state ID or a passport to be eligible to vote,” said State Senator Paula Hicks-Hudson (D). “Before you could have a utility bill or something like that. But now the law has been changed that you need either state ID, driver’s license, or a passport.
findings.note: Quoted by 13abc at a Lucas County early-voting press conference reminding voters of the new ID rules. She describes the change from a utility bill to a driver license, state ID or passport. The outlet attached a party letter to her name; it is not part of her words.
subjects: voter education on new ID law

findings.passage: I want to make sure that everyone knows that there are no new restrictions on voter ID at Early Voting.
findings.note: From her letter, issued as a state representative, to the Lucas County Board of Elections about HB 41 early-voting ID rules. She says in-person early voters can still vote without an ID in hand by giving the last four digits of their Social Security number in writing, and asks the board to train poll workers and call back voters wrongly turned away.
subjects: last four digits of Social Security number as ID

findings.passage: So, people can still go to Early Voting without an ID in their pocket and vote by providing their SSN+4 in writing.
findings.note: Same 2019 letter. She states that early voters without a photo or other ID may still vote by writing the last four digits of their Social Security number.

findings.passage: You can take a credit card anywhere in the world with a 4-digit pin and take out money, but we continue to restrict voting abilities while leveraging the under-resourced postal system to suppress our voters.
findings.note: Release on SB 293 (ends the grace period for mailed absentee ballots); the fetch tool returned it in two adjacent quoted segments, joined here. She compares voting checks to a card PIN.

findings.passage: In Lucas County, we know that it takes unreasonable extra days for our mail to be delivered across the street.
findings.note: Same release; gives her reason for opposing the mail-ballot deadline.

findings.passage: We don't have to worry about folks being removed from their roles because by voting, you're exercising your rights.
